artifact_observations.location: Right side of the spiral coil
artifact_observations.reasoning: Several loops of the spiral binding appear to merge into each other or lose their distinct circular geometry, looking like melted metal rather than distinct wire loops. This suggests a failure in maintaining consistent topology for repetitive structures.
The transition between the paper holes and the binding wire is slightly soft and indistinct, lacking the crisp physical separation expected in a macro photograph.
The background coils blur in a way that feels slightly inconsistent with optical bokeh, appearing more like a smudge than a gradual depth-of-field fall-off.

selected_experts.reason: To determine if the model considers a spiral-bound document as a 'binder' despite the taxonomy specifying ring mechanisms. This addresses the semantic gap.
To verify the structural integrity of the individual loops. AI often fails to keep repetitive thin structures separate, leading to fusion artifacts.
To assess the realism of the black and white conversion and the naturalness of the depth-of-field blur.
To check if the coil sits correctly on/through the paper planes without floating or intersecting incorrectly.

focus_areas: Structural integrity of the spiral loops (fusion/melting)

Semantic alignment of 'spiral notebook' vs 'ring binder'
